summary: In Greek mythology, Antiphus of Maeonia is son of Talaemenes and co-captain of the Maeonians with his brother Mesthles, allies of Priam born beneath Tmolus by the Gygaean lake. He is one of several Homeric and handbook Antiphuses and must not be merged with Antiphus son of Thessalus of Cos or with Priam's son Antiphus.

sections.heading: Maeonian captain
paragraphs: Homer sets Antiphus beside Mesthles at the head of the Maeonians; their mother was the nymph of the Gygaean lake, and they were born beneath Tmolus. Apollodorus names both sons of Talaemenes among the allies who joined the Trojans.
In the rally about Patroclus, Hector heartens Mesthles among the tribal captains; Antiphus remains a Catalogue co-leader rather than the focus of a private aristeia.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id antiphus-maeonian is the Maeonian son of Talaemenes alone. Distinct from antiphus-thessalus-cos (Heraclid captain of Cos), from Priam's son Antiphus, from Odysseus' crewman Antiphus, and from the many other Antiphuses on the Wikipedia disambiguation.
